pr_body:
Basically, it's Andy's [patch](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/e871d1f8b6d971d013eaa9e07c8a3fb907874239) that he never landed and asked me to (with some modifications).

Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/88021

```cpp
bool Test() => EqualityComparer<string>.Default.Equals("str", "str");
```
New codegen:
```asm
; Method Prog:Foo():bool:this
       mov      eax, 1
       ret      
; Total bytes of code: 6
```

It is also needed for https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/87847

Issue Details
Basically, it's Andy's patch that he never landed and asked me to. Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/88021 ```cpp bool Test() => EqualityComparer.Default.Equals("str", "str"); ``` New codegen: ```asm ; Method Prog:Foo():bool:this mov eax, 1 ret ; Total bytes of code: 6 ```
Author: EgorBo
Assignees: EgorBo
Labels: `area-CodeGen-coreclr`
Milestone: -

Wow I got some impressive performance improvements in my local benchmark.

But there's still some weird codegen which is unnecessary.

For example:

```csharp
bool Test() => new Foo(1, "hello", "test") == new Foo(1, "test", "hello");

record struct Foo(int x, string y, string z);
```

The codegen for `Test` is 
```asm
G_M50849_IG01:  ;; offset=0000H
						;; size=0 bbWeight=1.00 PerfScore 0.00
G_M50849_IG02:  ;; offset=0000H
       xor      eax, eax
       je       SHORT G_M50849_IG04
						;; size=4 bbWeight=1.00 PerfScore 1.25
G_M50849_IG03:  ;; offset=0004H
       xor      eax, eax
       jmp      SHORT G_M50849_IG05
						;; size=4 bbWeight=0.50 PerfScore 1.12
G_M50849_IG04:  ;; offset=0008H
       xor      eax, eax
						;; size=2 bbWeight=0.50 PerfScore 0.12
G_M50849_IG05:  ;; offset=000AH
       ret      
						;; size=1 bbWeight=1 PerfScore 1.00
```

which is effectively equivalent to:

```asm
       xor      eax, eax
       ret      
```

issue_context.title: EqualityComparer<string>.Default.Equals is never inlined
issue_context.body:
I was 100% sure I already filed an issue for this but I can't find it so filing _again_:
```cpp
bool Test() => EqualityComparer<string>.Default.Equals("str", "str");
```
Codegen:
```asm
; Method Prog:Foo():bool:this
G_M44901_IG01:  ;; offset=0000H
       sub      rsp, 40
       mov      rdx, 0x21700209268      ; 'str'
       mov      rcx, 0x21700209268      ; 'str'
       mov      r11, 0x7FF933EB0330
       call     [r11]System.IEquatable`1[System.__Canon]:Equals(System.__Canon):bool:this
       nop      
       add      rsp, 40
       ret      
; Total bytes of code: 43
```
Expected codegen:
```asm
; Method Prog:Foo():bool:this
       mov      eax, 1
       ret      
; Total bytes of code: 6
```
Even PGO doesn't help. In fact, it can be simulated as:

@jkotas yes, I was about to ask for help as I am a bit lost here, so for
```cs
bool Test() => EqualityComparer<string>.Default.Equals("str", "str");
```
when ILC compiles it, jit invokes [getMethodInfo](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1db4357891752cc028620710fe924425235b8f89/src/coreclr/tools/Common/JitInterface/CorInfoImpl.cs#L1182) like this:

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/assets/523221/1117afca-08d8-499f-8249-11c188cf4090)

and I don't know how I can use the context to get a proper method info

I tried `_compilation.TypeSystemContext.GetMethodForInstantiatedType(method, (InstantiatedType)ctxType)` but it complained that `method` should not be of `InstantiatedMethod`

also, tried `method.MakeInstantiatedMethod(ctx)`

Perhaps https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/88025/commits/1eddadb20d105e107cc28fca358632b2bcc00762 - at least it seems to instanciate correct types for my examples (for both when we have class and method context)

`entityFromContext` may return `MethodBeingCompiled` as a method context - I guess that's not what we want here when we invoke `getMethodInfo` for a random call inside current method - so I guarded the check with `context != contextFromMethodBeingCompiled()`

Although, the current CoreCLR is a bit more conservative - it ignores `context == currentMethodContext` and all methoddesc-like generics completely:

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/assets/523221/823942e1-130e-475e-a6a8-42fb7fe832a3)

so maybe I should align this here as well?

If JIT/EE interface method takes a `context` argument, I would expect it to be respected for all cases. People like to write complicated generics. Why not optimize all of them that we can optimize here?

FWIW, we rely heavily on generics for optimization in the JIT.
For example:

```
private static delegate*<ref SortingMatch<TInner>, Span<long>, int> 
    SortBy<TEntryComparer, TLookupKey, TFwdIt,TBackIt>(OrderMetadata metadata)
    where TEntryComparer : struct, IEntryComparer, IComparer<UnmanagedSpan>
    where TLookupKey : struct, ILookupKey
    where TFwdIt : struct,  ILookupIterator
    where TBackIt : struct, ILookupIterator
``

And many others where we are trying to get inlining for specialized impl

> If JIT/EE interface method takes a `context` argument, I would expect it to be respected for all cases. People like to write complicated generics. Why not optimize all of them that we can optimize here?

Added back to both - checked on CoreCLR and its impact on diffs was quite small compared to class ctx
```
